subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Does Tea Have Less Caffeine Than Coffee?
description: A 60-second lesson on Does Tea Have Less Caffeine Than Coffee?.

hook.text: People assume tea has less caffeine than coffee. Pound for pound, tea leaves actually contain MORE caffeine than coffee beans.

buildup.text: Dried tea leaves are about 3.5% caffeine by weight. Coffee beans are about 1.5%. Tea wins on concentration.

discovery.text: But you use far less tea per cup (2g) than coffee (10-15g). Less leaf per cup means less caffeine in the final drink.

twist.text: Tea also contains L-theanine, which moderates caffeine's effect. Tea drinkers feel alert but calm—not jittery like coffee.

climax.text: The 'tea has less caffeine' statement is true for the cup—but false for the leaf. Context determines the answer.

punchline.text: More caffeine in the leaf, less in the cup. Brewing ratio changes everything.

quiz.question: Why does a cup of tea have less caffeine than coffee despite tea leaves having more caffeine by weight?
options: Much less tea leaf (2g) is used per cup compared to coffee grounds (10-15g)
